passages.t: ‘Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion’
passages.happening:
Psalm 125 begins with a picture. “A song of ascents. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever” (verse 1). And a second picture: “As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people, both now and forevermore” (verse 2).

Then a promise. “For the scepter of the wicked will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous will not put forth their hands to injustice” (verse 3).

The singer prays, “Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart” (verse 4). But those who turn aside to crooked ways will be sent away with the evildoers. The psalm ends with a blessing: “Peace be upon Israel” (verse 5).
passages.hearers:
A pilgrim coming up to Jerusalem saw the city set on its ridges with higher hills around it, like arms around a child. The Mount of Olives rises to the east. The psalm turns that view into a picture of God around his people. The note on Psalm 120 explains the Songs of Ascents.

Mount Zion was first the name of the stronghold David captured (2 Samuel 5:7). It came to mean the temple hill and then the whole city as the place God had chosen.

A scepter was the rod a king held, a sign of his rule. Verse 3 seems to come from a time when an ungodly power ruled the land, or threatened to. Many scholars think of Judah after the exile, a small province under foreign governors. The verse sees a hidden danger: if the wicked ruled for long, even good people might start to go along with injustice. God will not let that rule last.

‘The land allotted’ recalls how the land was shared out among Israel's families by lot in Joshua's day, each portion a gift from God.
passages.later:
Isaiah heard God say, “Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you” (Isaiah 54:10). Jesus said of his sheep, “No one can snatch them out of My hand” (John 10:28).

Hebrews speaks of “an unshakable kingdom” that believers are receiving (Hebrews 12:28).
passages.hard: Does verse 4 mean God helps only those who deserve it? No. In this psalm ‘the good’ are described as “Those who trust in the LORD” (verse 1). Uprightness here is the direction of a life that leans on God, not a perfect record. Another Song of Ascents asks, “If You, O LORD, kept track of iniquities, then who, O Lord, could stand?” (Psalm 130:3).
passages.asks:
What makes you steady? Psalm 125 says that the one who trusts the LORD is like a mountain, not because he is strong, but because God is around him.

Verse 3 also asks something hard. When unjust people hold power for a long time, it is easy to start copying them. Where are you tempted to ‘put forth your hand’ to what is wrong, just because it seems to be how things work now?
